governanceNotes: SUDD/IBS diagnostic-overlap is the controlling guard: both constructs share low-grade inflammation and visceral hypersensitivity, so the mapping cannot adjudicate de novo IBS versus SUDD persistence; recorded for the qualified human with both literatures.

The colorectal-cancer association was screened and rejected: the 2022 meta-analysis (38,621 patients) found long-term colon-cancer risk after diverticulitis NOT increased (PMID 36042030); no edge is authored.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The IBS-diverticular-disease re-examination review states there is now epidemiological and pathophysiological evidence supporting de novo IBS development after an episode of acute diverticulitis, analogous to post-infection IBS after enteric illness (Alamo & Quigley 2019); the SUDD practical-guidance review characterizes the persistent post-episode symptom burden - chronic left-lower-quadrant pain with bowel-movement changes and low-grade inflammation impairing quality of life (Calini 2023); the management review notes potential similarities and overlap between diverticulitis and irritable-bowel-syndrome symptom complexes (Hanna & Kaiser 2021).
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established at the mapping level: post-diverticulitis IBS has epidemiological and pathophysiological support but no quantified incidence denominator in a general-population cohort; symptomatic uncomplicated diverticular disease (SUDD) and IBS remain diagnostically overlapping constructs sharing low-grade inflammation and visceral-hypersensitivity physiology, so persistent post-episode symptoms may represent SUDD rather than de novo IBS; Rome IV criteria require symptom documentation independent of the diverticular episode.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized post-inflammatory visceral-hypersensitivity pathway: an acute diverticulitis episode produces localized serosal and pericolic inflammation with low-grade immune activation; inflammatory mediators and altered gut microbiota sensitize enteric neurons and spinal afferents, producing persistent visceral hypersensitivity and dysmotility that outlasts the acute episode and meets IBS criteria. The same neuro-immune enteric interaction and muscular-dysfunction physiology characterizes SUDD, which is why the two syndromes are difficult to disentangle at the bedside.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Rome IV-positive IBS diagnosis documented after an acute, imaging-confirmed diverticulitis episode with a symptom-free interval; exclusion of SUDD, microscopic colitis, and bile-acid diarrhea; post-episode colonoscopy excluding complicated disease and alternative diagnoses where indicated
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Rome IV symptom-pattern documentation meeting IBS criteria following an imaging-confirmed acute diverticulitis episode; a documented symptom-free interval before IBS-type symptoms emerge; exclusion of SUDD, microscopic colitis, and bile-acid diarrhea
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Symptomatic uncomplicated diverticular disease (SUDD) rather than de novo IBS
Inflammatory bowel disease including SCAD mimic

evidenceGaps: Rome IV symptom-pattern documentation meeting IBS criteria following an imaging-confirmed acute diverticulitis episode
A documented symptom-free interval after the acute episode before IBS-type symptoms emerge (de novo pattern rather than persistence)
Exclusion of SUDD (same anatomic segment, low-grade calprotectin elevation), microscopic colitis, and bile-acid malabsorption
Exclusion of recurrent or smoldering diverticulitis driving the symptoms
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: de novo post-diverticulitis IBS has epidemiological and pathophysiological support but no quantified incidence cohort, and the SUDD/IBS diagnostic-overlap confound means persistent symptoms cannot be attributed to one construct over the other without specialist evaluation.

sourceReferences.citation: Alamo RZ, Quigley EMM. Irritable bowel syndrome and colonic diverticular disease: overlapping symptoms and overlapping therapeutic approaches. Curr Opin Gastroenterol. 2019;35(1):27-33. PMID 30407258.
sourceReferences.note: Re-examination review: epidemiological and pathophysiological evidence now supports de novo IBS development after an episode of acute diverticulitis, analogous to post-infection IBS; SUDD and IBS relationships remain debated with SUDD possibly distinguished by more frequent and severe pain.

sourceReferences.note: SUDD guidance: chronic condition impairing quality of life with persistent left-lower-quadrant pain, bowel-movement changes and low-grade inflammation (elevated calprotectin) without systemic inflammation; pathogenesis involves microbiota alterations, neuro-immune enteric interactions and muscular dysfunction.
